editor_note: Entry 6 is faithful and natural. It keeps every caveat ("uniquement", "version préliminaire", "susceptibles de changer") and the three plan names. Entry 18 keeps the meaning but has two style problems. "Estimation atténuée des erreurs d'une observable O" is clumsy: it says the estimation is mitigated, not the observable's errors, and "Estimation d'une observable O avec atténuation des erreurs" reads better. "Carte de bruit" copies the English "noise map"; "application de bruit" is the usual French term, though "carte" is at least consistent with entries 12 and 17. "Contracté ... de l'intérieur vers l'extérieur" for "from the middle out" is acceptable, and "à partir du milieu vers les bords" would be more precise.

examples.source: Error-mitigated estimation of an observable O via post-processing measurement outcomes
examples.translation: Estimation atténuée des erreurs d'une observable O via le post-traitement des résultats de mesure
examples.suggested: Estimation d'une observable O avec atténuation des erreurs, par post-traitement des résultats de mesure
examples.why: The compound adjective 'error-mitigated' is copied word for word from the English. 'Estimation atténuée' makes it sound as if the estimation itself is attenuated.

examples.source: the associated noise map
examples.translation: la carte de bruit associée
examples.suggested: l'application de bruit associée (ou le canal de bruit associé)
examples.why: In French quantum-information writing, a 'map' is an 'application' (or 'canal' for a noise channel). 'Carte' is a recognizable calque, not a false concept, and it matches entries 12 and 17.

editor_note: Faithful and natural across all five short entries: "skills" is rendered consistently as "compétences" (a defensible choice for agent skills), "changelog" as "Journal des modifications", and entry [5] keeps both the release and the migration purpose ("a été publiée, pour migrer le code `qiskit-ibm-runtime`").

The meaning is faithful all through, and nothing would mislead a learner. The "might be faster" hedge is kept as "pourraient être plus rapides", and the informal register holds ("Consulte", "visite", "Lis"). Two small polish points are in entry [9]. "du Qiskit SDK" keeps the English word order where French would say "du SDK Qiskit". "Qiskit patterns" is a named Qiskit framework concept, and the generic "modèles" hides that reference.

examples.source: the latest transpilation capabilities from the Qiskit SDK
examples.translation: les dernières capacités de transpilation du Qiskit SDK
examples.suggested: les dernières capacités de transpilation du SDK Qiskit
examples.why: This copies the English word order. French puts the generic noun first (SDK Qiskit).

examples.source: integrate the service into their current Qiskit patterns and workflows
examples.translation: intégrer facilement le service dans leurs modèles et workflows Qiskit actuels
examples.suggested: intégrer facilement le service dans leurs Qiskit patterns et workflows actuels
examples.why: "Qiskit patterns" is a named framework in the Qiskit docs. The generic "modèles" hides that reference, though the meaning survives.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful and nothing would mislead a learner. The "tu" register holds ("Écris", "Consulte", "Lis") and core terms are correct (passes de transpilation, mesure projective conjointe, tolérante aux pannes). A native editor would still fix a few calques. "Qiskit SDK" keeps English word order ("du Qiskit SDK") where French says "du SDK Qiskit". "early fault-tolerant" becomes the awkward "tolérance aux pannes précoce". "Rust-driven" is calqued as "pilotées par Rust", and "release summaries" as the stiff "résumés de publication".

examples.source: The latest updates from Qiskit SDK, including the latest package release summaries
examples.translation: Les dernières mises à jour du Qiskit SDK, y compris les derniers résumés de publication des packages
examples.suggested: Les dernières mises à jour du SDK Qiskit, y compris les résumés des dernières versions des packages
examples.why: French puts the noun first ("SDK Qiskit"), and "résumés de publication" is a stiff calque. The same English word order appears in [1] and [15].

examples.source: Improvements in early fault-tolerant transpilation ... early fault-tolerant targets
examples.translation: Améliorations de la transpilation en tolérance aux pannes précoce ... cibles à tolérance aux pannes précoce
examples.suggested: Améliorations de la transpilation pour les premières machines tolérantes aux pannes ... cibles tolérantes aux pannes de première génération
examples.why: "early" refers to the first generation of fault-tolerant machines. Here it reads as if the fault tolerance itself is premature, which is clumsy but still understandable.

examples.source: Rust-driven performance enhancements
examples.translation: des améliorations de performance pilotées par Rust
examples.suggested: des gains de performance grâce à une réécriture en Rust
examples.why: "pilotées par Rust" is a literal calque of "Rust-driven". A French technical writer would not phrase it this way.

examples.source: To see the release notes for all versions
examples.translation: Pour consulter les notes de version de toutes les versions
examples.suggested: Pour consulter les notes de toutes les versions
examples.why: "notes de version de toutes les versions" repeats the word "version" and reads awkwardly.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The 32-digit feature code, the seven-digit verification code, the 10 minutes per 28-day rolling window, the affiliation and course-name trick in the name fields, and the "not activated without this final step" caveat all come through intact. A native editor would still fix three phrasings. The IBM plan name "Open Plan" is translated as "Plan Ouvert" when it should stay as the product name. "Vérifie ta boîte de réception pour un code" is calqued from the English. "Visite https://…" reads unnaturally for a URL instruction. The informal "tu" register is used consistently.

examples.source: under the Open Plan ... The Open Plan provides 10 minutes
examples.translation: dans le cadre du Plan Ouvert ... Le Plan Ouvert offre 10 minutes
examples.suggested: dans le cadre de l'Open Plan ... L'Open Plan offre 10 minutes
examples.why: 'Open Plan' is the name of an IBM Quantum plan and appears in English on the platform. Translating it makes it harder to match against the UI and pricing pages.

examples.source: Check your email inbox for a seven-digit verification code
examples.translation: Vérifie ta boîte de réception pour un code de vérification à sept chiffres
examples.suggested: Consulte ta boîte de réception pour y trouver le code de vérification à sept chiffres
examples.why: 'Vérifier X pour un code' copies the English 'check X for'. It is not idiomatic French.

examples.source: Visit https://cloud.ibm.com/.
examples.translation: Visite https://cloud.ibm.com/.
examples.suggested: Rends-toi sur https://cloud.ibm.com/.
examples.why: 'Visiter' with a URL is a calque. 'Rends-toi sur' or 'Va sur' is the usual wording in French documentation.

editor_note: Entry 9 is faithful and uses the tu register correctly ("Remarque que si tu actives le Pauli-twirling dans ton job Sampler…"). It keeps the condition and says the total shots depend on `num_randomizations` and `shots_per_randomization`, and it stays consistent with the page's job/shots usage.

Nothing here would mislead a learner, and the page uses the informal "tu" throughout, but three small things are worth fixing. The page title [1] and the body [0], [5] keep "Open source", while the H1 [3] translates it as "Source ouverte". That is inconsistent, and "Source ouverte" is unusual in French technical writing. In [4], "dynamic and welcoming group" became "groupe ouvert et accueillant": "dynamic" was swapped for "ouvert", probably because "dynamique" had already been used for "vibrant" in the sentence before. In [6], "from code in pull requests" lost the word "code", which flattens the contrast between code contributions and community support.

examples.source: Open source {#open-source}
examples.translation: Source ouverte {#open-source}
examples.suggested: Open source {#open-source}
examples.why: The page title [1] and body [0], [5] use 'open source'. The heading translates it differently, which is inconsistent and uncommon in French technical writing.

examples.source: a dynamic and welcoming group of developers
examples.translation: un groupe ouvert et accueillant de développeurs
examples.suggested: un groupe dynamique et accueillant de développeurs (et rendre « vibrant community » par « communauté active »)
examples.why: The adjective 'dynamic' was replaced by 'ouvert'. The change is small but it does not match the source.

examples.source: from code in pull requests to community support on Slack
examples.translation: des pull requests au soutien communautaire sur [Slack]
examples.suggested: du code soumis via des pull requests au soutien communautaire sur [Slack]
examples.why: Dropping 'code' weakens the contrast between technical contributions and community ones.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and natural: [27] keeps "implémentation plus sophistiquée … sous forme de service cloud" with "atténuation des erreurs", and [34] keeps the hedge ("tu pourrais accéder plus facilement") and translates "toggling" as "en activant des options telles que le resilience_level", using the informal "tu".

Neither rewritten entry misleads a reader. Entry 24 keeps every caveat: "peut dépendre à la fois", "Dans certains cas", "peuvent atteindre une qualité de solution finale similaire" and "l'ensemble du flux de travail d'optimisation" all match the English, so it is fine as written. Entry 8 translates software "requirements" as "développé avec les exigences suivantes", which is a calque. A French technical writer would say "prérequis" or "configuration requise" for a list of package versions.

examples.source: The code on this page was developed using the following requirements.
examples.translation: Le code de cette page a été développé avec les exigences suivantes.
examples.suggested: Le code de cette page a été développé avec les prérequis suivants.
examples.why: "Exigences" is a literal calque of software "requirements". "Prérequis" or "configuration requise" is the usual French term for a list of dependency versions.

editor_note: Entry 8 keeps the meaning, including "ces versions ou des versions plus récentes", and would not mislead a learner. One wording choice is a calque: "développé avec les exigences suivantes" translates "requirements" word for word. For a list of package versions, a French technical writer would say "prérequis" or "configuration requise", not "exigences".

examples.source: The code on this page was developed using the following requirements.
examples.translation: Le code de cette page a été développé avec les exigences suivantes.
examples.suggested: Le code de cette page a été développé avec les prérequis suivants.
examples.why: In French, 'exigences' reads as demands or specifications. For a list of package versions, the usual word is 'prérequis' or 'configuration requise'. The meaning is still clear, so this is minor.

editor_note: Entry 6 keeps the English meaning, including the "typically" hedge ("généralement insérée"). "réinitialisation implicite" is right, and "le drapeau `init_qubits`" defined as an "option d'exécution de primitive" is also correct and matches the surrounding entries' QPU/réinitialisation wording.

The meaning is faithful all the way through. The IBM-vs-user split of responsibilities is kept, including the "IBM n'est pas responsable de la sauvegarde…" disclaimers, and the "tu" register holds. A few spots read like translated English. In [15], "S'assurer que des données personnelles et réglementées ne sont pas fournies" follows the English word order and is stiff. In [17], "si disponible" and "tâches impactées" are anglicisms. Also in [17], "jobs" becomes "tâches", which is the same word as the "Tâche" column header, so the two can blur.

examples.source: Ensure that personal and regulated data is not provided.
examples.translation: S'assurer que des données personnelles et réglementées ne sont pas fournies.
examples.suggested: S'assurer qu'aucune donnée personnelle ou réglementée n'est fournie.
examples.why: This copies the English negation structure. French would put the negation on the data itself ("aucune donnée") and use "ou" instead of "et".

examples.source: Resubmit any impacted jobs following recovery.
examples.translation: Soumettre à nouveau les tâches impactées après la récupération.
examples.suggested: Soumettre à nouveau les jobs concernés après le rétablissement du service.
examples.why: "Impactées" is an anglicism. Rendering "jobs" as "tâches" also clashes with the table's "Tâche" column header. Elsewhere Qiskit French docs usually keep "job".

examples.source: in an alternate region, if available.
examples.translation: dans une autre région, si disponible.
examples.suggested: dans une autre région, le cas échéant.
examples.why: "Si disponible" copies "if available" word for word. "Le cas échéant" or "si possible" is the natural French wording.

editor_note: The meaning is accurate throughout: 20 questions, at least 16 correct to pass, lock after two failed attempts, and the Credly privacy notice are all preserved, so nothing would mislead a learner. Entry [8] has a real grammar error: "tu dois en répondre correctement à au moins 16" puts "en" and "à" together, which French does not allow. Some phrases are calques a native editor would change: "Félicitations pour avoir terminé" should be "Félicitations d'avoir terminé", "réclamer ton badge" should be "récupérer ton badge", and "note de passage" is Canadian usage where France would say "note suffisante". The course title is left in English in [5] ("Basics of Quantum Information") but translated in [7] ("Les bases de l'information quantique").

examples.source: you must answer at least 16 correctly to pass
examples.translation: tu dois en répondre correctement à au moins 16 pour réussir
examples.suggested: tu dois répondre correctement à au moins 16 d'entre elles pour réussir
examples.why: "en" cannot be used together with "répondre à". The sentence is ungrammatical, though the meaning is still clear.

examples.source: Congratulations on completing the "Basics of Quantum Information" course
examples.translation: Félicitations pour avoir terminé le cours "Basics of Quantum Information"
examples.suggested: Félicitations d'avoir terminé le cours « Les bases de l'information quantique »
examples.why: "Félicitations d'avoir" is the natural French construction. The title is also left in English here but translated in [7].

examples.source: instructions for claiming the badge
examples.translation: les instructions pour réclamer ton badge
examples.suggested: les instructions pour récupérer ton badge
examples.why: "Réclamer" is a calque of "claim" and suggests complaining or demanding. "Récupérer" is the normal word here.

examples.source: If you don't receive a passing score
examples.translation: Si tu n'obtiens pas une note de passage
examples.suggested: Si tu n'obtiens pas la note minimale requise
examples.why: "Note de passage" is Canadian usage. In France, readers would expect "note minimale" or "réussir l'examen".

editor_note: Entry 29 (Credly privacy notice) says the same thing as the English and keeps "tu" throughout, but several phrases are calqued from English. "Data processor" is rendered "processeur de données"; in French data-protection language (RGPD) the standard term is "sous-traitant (de données)". "Instructions pour réclamer le badge" and "IBM exploite les services" copy "claim" and "leverages" word for word, and "à des fins de reporting et opérationnelles du programme" is stiff. Separately, the period was moved inside the link text ("[ici.]"), which is a small markup slip.

examples.source: a third-party data processor authorized by IBM
examples.translation: un processeur de données tiers autorisé par IBM
examples.suggested: un sous-traitant tiers autorisé par IBM
examples.why: In French data-protection language (RGPD), a 'data processor' is a 'sous-traitant'. 'Processeur de données' is a literal calque.

examples.source: with instructions for claiming the badge
examples.translation: avec des instructions pour réclamer le badge
examples.suggested: avec les instructions pour récupérer ton badge
examples.why: 'Réclamer' suggests demanding something you are owed. 'Récupérer' is the natural French verb here.

examples.source: IBM leverages the services of Credly ... for program reporting and operational purposes
examples.translation: IBM exploite les services de Credly ... à des fins de reporting et opérationnelles du programme
examples.suggested: IBM fait appel aux services de Credly ... à des fins de suivi et de gestion opérationnelle du programme
examples.why: 'Exploite' copies 'leverages' word for word, and the adjective chain 'de reporting et opérationnelles du programme' reads awkwardly in French.

editor_note: In rewritten entry 71 the double-angle identities are kept verbatim, and the prose "En résumé, l'état du registre $\mathsf{Q}$ au début de l'étape 2 est" matches the English exactly and flows into entry 73 without any drift.

The translation is faithful and reads naturally, using "modèle de requête" and "boîte de Pétri" consistently, keeping the rigid/unnatural caveat, rendering Simon's "plus robuste et plus convaincant" advantage correctly and using the informal "te guide / Télécharge" throughout.
Rewritten entry 15 is faithful: "Answer"→"Réponse", "Four."→"Quatre.", which matches the four-wire circuit in the question in entry 14, and the Accordion markup is left intact.

None of the three rewritten entries (5, 8, 12) would mislead a learner. The pass threshold in [8] ("au moins 16 d'entre elles" out of 20) matches the English, and the Credly notice in [12] keeps every data-sharing caveat, with "data processor" correctly rendered as "sous-traitant". Two small style points: [5] says "améliorer" twice in a row where the English uses improve/enhance, and "réclamer ton badge" in [12] is a calque of "claim". The informal "tu" register is used throughout.

examples.source: Your feedback will be used to enhance our content offering and user experience.
examples.translation: Tes retours seront utilisés pour améliorer notre offre de contenu et l'expérience utilisateur.

examples.why: 'améliorer' was already used in the sentence before, and the passive 'seront utilisés pour' is stiff.

examples.source: with instructions for claiming the badge
examples.translation: avec les instructions pour réclamer ton badge
examples.suggested: avec les instructions pour récupérer ton badge
examples.why: 'réclamer' copies 'claim' and suggests demanding something owed. 'Récupérer' or 'accepter' sounds more natural in French.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning: optimization levels 0/1 (default 1), the 0–3 range in other contexts, and skip_transpilation because the pass manager already transpiled the circuit. Entry 37 slips into the formal register with "consultez", while entry 36 uses the informal "consulte" and "ton circuit" as the page convention requires. Entry 37 also writes "l'Estimator" with an article, but entry 36 writes bare "Estimator", so the primitive's name is handled two ways in adjacent paragraphs.

examples.source: To learn about resilience level settings, refer to the [documentation]
examples.translation: Pour en savoir plus sur les paramètres de niveau de résilience, consultez la [documentation]
examples.suggested: Pour en savoir plus sur les paramètres de niveau de résilience, consulte la [documentation]

examples.suggested: Résilience intégrée d'Estimator : comme pour l'optimisation, Estimator dispose de paramètres intégrés

editor_note: Rewritten entry 67 is accurate and uses the informal "tu" ("consulte ce guide"): Estimator stays in English, and "valeur propre d'énergie la plus basse", "erreur standard de l'ensemble" and "fonction de coût" are all rendered correctly, with no drift.

The meaning is faithful throughout, the terms are correct (noyaux quantiques, circuits quantiques variationnels, encodage des données) and "tu" is used consistently. A few phrasings are calqued from English and a native editor would rewrite them. In [4], "offrira une révision de certaines approches … supposera également une certaine familiarité" reads stiffly. In [6], the passive "tu seras notifié par Credly" copies the English structure, and in [11], "réclamer ton badge" is a literal rendering of "claiming the badge".

examples.source: The course will offer some review of classical machine learning approaches, but will also assume some familiarity with these methods.
examples.translation: Le cours offrira une révision de certaines approches classiques de l'apprentissage automatique, mais supposera également une certaine familiarité avec ces méthodes.

examples.why: 'offrir une révision' and 'supposer une familiarité' are calques; the native phrasing is 'passer en revue' plus a direct clause.

examples.source: you will be notified by Credly that you have earned a badge.
examples.translation: tu seras notifié par Credly que tu as obtenu un badge.
examples.suggested: Credly t'informera que tu as obtenu un badge.
examples.why: French avoids this English-style passive; the active voice is more natural.

examples.source: instructions for claiming the badge
examples.translation: les instructions pour réclamer ton badge
examples.suggested: les instructions pour récupérer ton badge
examples.why: 'réclamer' suggests complaining or demanding; 'récupérer' (or 'accepter') is the usual wording for collecting a badge.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and nothing in it would mislead a learner. Core terms are correct and used the same way throughout: suppression/atténuation/détection/correction des erreurs, tolérante aux fautes, and twirling de Pauli, with "noise tailoring" glossed as "mise en forme du bruit". There are two small wording slips. In [5], "Roughly speaking" becomes "En résumé", which drops the hint that the three definitions are only approximate. In [11], "bring quantum advantage within reach" is shortened to a vague "rapprocher l'avantage quantique".

examples.source: Roughly speaking:
examples.translation: En résumé :
examples.suggested: Schématiquement :

editor_note: All three rewritten entries (5, 7, 11) keep the meaning and use "tu" throughout. Nothing would mislead a learner, and the Credly notice keeps every caveat: third-party processor, US location, data shared, global sharing. Two small edits a native editor would make. In entry 11, "instructions pour réclamer le badge" copies English "claim". "Réclamer" suggests demanding or complaining, so "récupérer" reads better. In entry 7, the course title appears without quotes ("le badge pour Utiliser un ordinateur quantique aujourd'hui"), while entry 5 puts it in « », and the bare title after "pour" reads awkwardly.

examples.source: with instructions for claiming the badge
examples.translation: avec des instructions pour réclamer le badge
examples.suggested: avec les instructions pour récupérer ton badge
examples.why: "Réclamer" copies English "claim" and suggests demanding or complaining; "récupérer" is the usual French wording for collecting a badge.

examples.suggested: passer l'examen du badge « Utiliser un ordinateur quantique aujourd'hui »

editor_note: Entry 32 ("Lorsque nous appliquons $H$ aux états $|+\rangle$ et $|+\rangle$, nous obtenons :") is a faithful, natural rendering with the math intact. Its duplicated $|+\rangle$ (which should be $|-\rangle$) comes from the English source, so it is an upstream typo and not a translation defect.

Entries 4 and 5 are faithful and natural French. "undergraduate-level" is rendered as "niveau licence", QKD as "distribution quantique de clés (QKD)", and the free-time caveat as "au cas où les étudiants épuiseraient accidentellement leur temps de calcul quantique gratuit", which keeps the meaning intact.

Entry 21 keeps the English meaning. Measuring along the same axis still gives perfectly anti-correlated results (up/down, into/out of the page), and letting the observers choose any direction is still what makes the statistics interesting. "Players" becomes "participants", which matches entry 45. The one thing to fix is "l'un obtient up, l'autre obtient down": a bare English "up"/"down" as the object of "obtient" reads awkwardly in French. Entry 17 says "spin up/down", so "obtient un spin up … un spin down" would read better here and would also match the parallel "obtient un spin rentrant dans la page" in the same sentence.

examples.line_approx: every time one measures up, the other measures down

examples.suggested: chaque fois que l'un obtient un spin up, l'autre obtient un spin down

editor_note: All five rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. The anticorrelation in [79] ("on est sûr de trouver l'autre dans l'état |1⟩") and the collapse caveat in [159] ("la mesure fait s'effondrer leur état et détruit la superposition") keep their meaning, [189] "Optimisation" matches the step list, and every entry uses tu.

Both rewritten entries are faithful and nothing in them would mislead a learner. Entry 4 keeps every point from the English: the Open Plan free time, "bien moins de temps que celui alloué gratuitement" and the simulator fallback. It also renders "such as uncertainty and superposition" correctly. Two modal shifts are worth a small fix. In entry 7, the hedged "might be most effective" became the certain "où il sera le plus utile", where "serait" would match the English. In entry 4, the advisory "should be started in class" became the stronger "doit être commencé", where "devrait" would match.

examples.suggested: l'endroit du cursus où il serait le plus efficace
examples.why: The English hedges with 'might be', but the French states it as certain. The meaning is only slightly off, so this is minor.

editor_note: Entry 6 is faithful throughout. Every description keeps its meaning, for example "Rétropropagation d'opérateur pour réduire la profondeur du circuit", "Diagonalisation quantique par échantillonnage" and "surcoût d'échantillonnage de la PEC". The one defect is the addon name in the first row, which appears as "**circuit Cutting**" with a stray lowercase "c". It looks like an artifact of automated casing. The proper name should be restored to "**Circuit Cutting**" as in the English, or fully translated as "**Découpe de circuit**".

examples.suggested: | **Circuit Cutting** | `qiskit-addon-cutting` |
examples.why: The broken capitalization of the addon's proper name looks like a mechanical artifact. It does not mislead, but a native editor would fix it.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The trade-off numbers (16% lower two-qubit depth, 9% higher gate count), the caveat about SABRE on individual circuits and the limits of mirror circuits all come through correctly. What remains is register and naturalness. The prerequisite links [10]/[11] use the vous imperative ("Transpilez", "Configurez"). "Requirements" [22] is rendered "Prérequis", the same word as [9]. A few English calques read stiffly: "tu pourrais être intéressé par le matériel suivant" [64], "le support de visualisation" [24], "reste pratique" [60] and "entraîné à optimiser" [39].

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and natural: [7] "valeurs d'espérance de plusieurs observables sur un balayage de paramètres en un seul appel" and [38] "évaluer un circuit paramétré pour de nombreuses valeurs de paramètres en un seul appel" match the English and keep the page's terminology ("balayage", "primitive Estimator", "retourne", as in [51]); the capitalized "Circuit" in [38] is left to the separate leak sweep.

The meaning is faithful throughout, and the core terms are correct and used the same way every time (ensemble indépendant maximum, démarrage à chaud itératif, mixeurs XY, variable d'écart, contraintes deux à deux). There are three small slips. [5] uses the formal "Votre temps d'exécution" where the page otherwise uses "tu". [49] adds "nativement", which the English does not have, and refers to the masculine `OptimizationProblem` as "elle". [50] "natif au" is an awkward calque.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 39 is faithful and natural: "un problème d'échantillonnage adapté à l'exécution avec la primitive SamplerV2" and "le StatevectorSampler de qiskit.primitives pour la simulation locale" match the English exactly, and "primitive" is used the same way as in entries 9 and 15.

The five rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally, with the caveat kept in entry 4 ("il s'agit d'une estimation uniquement", "Ton temps d'exécution peut varier"), "une erreur qui s'annule lorsque $\delta_\tau \to 0$" in entry 33, and "décomposition en portes" and "portes SWAP pour gérer la connectivité des qubits" in entries 47 and 48.

None of the 11 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The commutation example in [42] ([XX,IX]=0, IZ anti-commutes, two circuits instead of one), the caveat about truncation error in [18] and the noiseless-versus-noisy claim in [57] all match the English, and 'valeur moyenne' and 'rétropropagation' are used consistently. What remains is phrasing. In [64], 'le matériel suivant' is a calque of 'material' and should be 'les ressources suivantes'. In [59], 'obtenons la valeur moyenne idéale à ≃0,89' is clumsy. Also in [59], writing '0,89' inside LaTeX math mode puts a space after the comma, so it displays as '0, 89' unless it is written '0{,}89'.

examples.source: you might be interested in the following material

editor_note: One sentence changes the meaning. In [62], "coherence times and gate fidelities vary across a device" (from qubit to qubit on one chip) becomes "varient d'un appareil à l'autre" (from one device to another). That removes the reason the passage gives for why the choice of physical qubits matters. The rest is faithful, but the register is split: "tu" in [18], [31] and [38], against "vous/Notez/Consultez" in [65], [66], [71], [88], [131], [141], [142], [149], [152] and [155]. Several terms are also inconsistent: "surcoût" vs "surcharge d'échantillonnage" in [86], "ombre" vs "nuances" for "shade" ([17] vs [86]), "flux de travail" vs "workflow", and both "la PEC" and "le PEC". In [82], "supported on more qubits" is rendered as the software sense "pris en charge" instead of the mathematical support of an operator.

examples.source: because coherence times and gate fidelities vary across a device and drift over time
examples.translation: car les temps de cohérence et les fidélités des portes varient d'un appareil à l'autre et dérivent dans le temps
examples.suggested: car les temps de cohérence et les fidélités des portes varient d'un qubit à l'autre sur un même appareil et dérivent dans le temps
examples.why: The English means variation within one device, which is why picking the physical qubits matters. The French says variation between devices, which no longer explains why qubit selection matters.

examples.why: 'Supported on' refers to the mathematical support of an operator. 'Pris en charge' reads as software support.

examples.source: The computed shades are upper bounds ... reduces the sampling overhead.
examples.translation: Les nuances calculées sont des bornes supérieures ... ne fait que rendre les bornes plus lâches (trivial) ... réduit davantage la surcharge d'échantillonnage.
examples.suggested: Les ombres calculées sont des bornes supérieures ... plus lâches (triviales) ... réduit davantage le surcoût d'échantillonnage.
examples.why: This entry uses 'nuances' for 'shade' and 'surcharge' for 'overhead', while the rest of the file uses 'ombre' and 'surcoût'. 'trivial' should also agree with 'bornes' (triviales).

examples.why: The file mixes 'vous' here and in [65], [66], [71], [88], [141], [142], [149], [152] and [155] with 'tu' in [18], [31] and [38]. The convention is informal 'tu'.

examples.source: Only on qubit 6 ... does a Z error fail to commute, while an X error does commute.
examples.translation: Seulement sur le qubit 6, où nous initialisons l'état propre +1 de la base X, une erreur Z ne parvient pas à commuter, tandis qu'une erreur X commute.
examples.suggested: Ce n'est que sur le qubit 6, où nous préparons l'état propre +1 de la base X, qu'une erreur Z ne commute pas, alors qu'une erreur X commute.
examples.why: 'Ne parvient pas à commuter' is a literal copy of 'fail to commute', and the sentence uses 'Seulement ...' where 'Ce n'est que ... que' is the natural French construction.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The Trotter, Krylov-basis, sparsity and upper-bound claims all match the English. What a native editor would still change: the register slips to "vous" in [0] "Utilisez", [4] "Votre temps d'exécution" and [47] "consultez", while the rest of the page uses "tu". Terms are also inconsistent: "SQD Qiskit addon" is "addon SQD" in [6]/[66] but "Module complémentaire SQD" in [41], and "sample-based" is "basée sur l'échantillonnage" in [10] but "basée sur les échantillons" everywhere else. [61] "est garantie d'être une borne supérieure" is a calque.

editor_note: Entry 79 is faithful and reads naturally. "Cours IBM Quantum [Fundamentals of Quantum Algorithms] du Dr John Watrous" keeps the course title in English, as entries 15 and 23 do, and "Dr" without a period follows French typography.

The meaning is faithful throughout: I found no inverted conditions, swapped quantities or invented claims, and the segment counts (3+2, 6+4) and fidelity figures all match the source. The most important fix is "inline", which is calqued as "en ligne" in [27] and [81]. In French that means "online", so a reader could think the original tutorial runs online, when it actually writes the steps out directly in the notebook. The term "twirling" appears in four different forms: "twirling de Pauli" [53], "torsion de porte" [59], "brouillage de Pauli" [82], and "par torsion" inside the TREX expansion [53]. The file also switches between "workflow" and "flux de travail", between "étapes"/"pas de Trotter" [72] and between "coup de neutron" and "kick" [47]. The headings "Exemple de simulateur/matériel à grande échelle" are calqued from the English.
